Date July 26, 19 27/7 38.

Subject ASSISTANCE TO JAPANESE GENDARMERIE.

Made by D.S.I. NALLAEVSKY Forwarded by D.I. GROVER.

Sir,

Further to my report submitted on July 18th 1938, I have to state that enquiries made at the Wei Chung (惠中) Hotel at 515 Hankow Road revealed that at about 12 noon on June 30th. 1938 two male Chinese came to the Hotel and engaged a room No. 104 in the name of one Woo Yih Sung (吴一生) 41, Shanghai, Merchant. They remained in the room for about half an hour and then left. At about 3 o'clock in the same afternoon these two Chinese came back to the Hotel in company with 3 Japanese and a Russian and stayed in the room until about 6.30 p.m. and then went away.

According to the Russian informer he was to come to this room, during this afternoon, together with four arrested persons, under the pretext of selling them Vansers, and have them apprehended.

The four men were arrested on July 1st. 1938 and since when are detained at S.B.H.Q. (C.I).

As no evidence has been obtained to connect these persons with offences committed against the Japanese Military Authorities instructions regarding their disposal hereby, respectfully, requested.

日期：1938年7月26日 27/7 38。

事由：协助日本宪兵队。

由副督察长 NALLAEVSKY 呈报，经督察长 GROVER 转呈。

先生：

继我于1938年7月18日提交的报告之后，兹陈述如下：在汉口路515号惠中酒店（Wei Chung Hotel）进行的查询显示，1938年6月30日中午12时许，两名中国男子来到该酒店，以吴一生（Woo Yih Sung），41岁，上海，商人的名义预订了104号房间。他们在房间内停留了约半小时后离开。同日下午3时许，这两名中国人与3名日本人和1名俄罗斯人一同返回酒店，并在房间内停留至下午6时30分左右，随后离去。

据该俄罗斯线人称，他将于当天下午与四名被捕人员一同前往该房间，借口向他们出售“Vansers”（原文不清，可能指某种物品或武器），并将他们逮捕。

这四名男子于1938年7月1日被捕，此后一直拘押在特别处总部（刑事科）。

由于未能获得将这些人与针对日本军事当局所犯罪行联系起来的证据，特此恭敬地请求关于处置他们的指示。

Subject ASSISTANCE TO JAPANESE GENDARMERIE.

Made by D.S.I. MAKIAEVSKY    Forwarded by D.I. GLOVER.

Sir,

Statements of all concerned have now been taken
down and are forwarded with this report.

There seems to be no evidence whatsoever against
the four arrested men to show that any of them was connected with
any anti-Japanese activities. The Russian informer in his
statement said that Chang Zeng Kwang (張成光), 1st. arrested
man, was the commander of the Chinese mobile unit, who had just
arrived in Shanghai for the special purpose of purchasing
firearms for his unit which was operating somewhere 300 miles
away from Shanghai. Subsequent enquiries made revealed that
Chang Zeng Kwang is a former C.P.W.2075, who first registered
with the S.M.P. on December 12, 1929, being recommended by
C.P.C.2108. On July 12th. 1932, he obtained a position of a
watchman at the Sun Co. Yu Ya Ching Road, which he held until
November 30, 1934. On the above date he was re-engaged as a
private watchman No.1 and remained with the Sun Co. until Aug.
1937, when he resigned due to refusal by the management of
frequent applications for leave of absence. Upon his resignation
he was given a bonus of $50.00 for good services. He was very
highly attested by the manager when interviewed by detectives.

On August 31st. 1937, he obtained, through the S.M.P.
a position of a Police Watchman with the Kiangsu Chemical Works,
at 181 Ferry Road, which he held until November 30th. 1937, when
he resigned due to bad health. Shortly after his resignation,
he, together with a friend of his, one Tsan Ching Feng (趙俊峯)
now Detective Sergeant attached to the First Squad of the
Detective Bureau of the Da Dao Government in Pootung, established
a transportation company under the name of Pah Chi. (伯記)

报告
日期：1938年7月19日。

事由：协助日本宪兵队。

由副督察长 MAKIAEVSKY 呈报，经督察长 GLOVER 转呈。

先生：

所有相关人员的供词现已记录在案，并随本报告一并转呈。

似乎没有任何证据表明这四名被捕人员中的任何一人与任何反日活动有关。该俄罗斯线人在其供词中称，第一名被捕人员张成光（Chang Zeng Kwang，原文拼写有误，应为Chang Zing Kwang）是中国流动部队（Chinese mobile unit）的指挥官，他刚抵达上海，专门目的是为其在距离上海约300英里处活动的部队购买枪支。随后的调查显示，张成光是前巡捕编号2075（C.P.W.2075），他于1929年12月12日首次在上海公共租界工部局警务处注册，由巡捕编号2108（C.P.C.2108）推荐。1932年7月12日，他在虞洽卿路（Yu Ya Ching Road）孙公司（Sun Co.）获得了一份看门人的职位，一直任职至1934年11月30日。在上述日期，他被重新聘为1号私人看门人，并留在孙公司直至1937年8月，当时因管理层拒绝其频繁请假申请而辞职。辞职时，因其服务良好，获发奖金50.00美元。侦探在问询时，经理对他评价极高。

1937年8月31日，他通过上海公共租界工部局警务处在渡边路（Ferry Road）181号的江苏化学厂（Kiangsu Chemical Works）获得了一份警察看门人的职位，一直任职至1937年11月30日，后因健康不佳辞职。辞职后不久，他与一位朋友赵俊峯（Tsan Ching Feng，现为大刀政府浦东侦探局第一小队侦探警长）共同成立了一家名为伯記（Pah Chi）的运输公司。

Transportation Company with temporary offices at Room No.406
of the Chung Nan Hotel, 560 Avenue Edward VII.

The company was liquidated in March 1938 owing to bad
business and Chang Zeng Kwang with the assistance of his friend
Tsau Ching Feng (趙俊峯) obtained a position of a Detective
with the Detective Bureau of the Tai Dao Government at the pay
of $20.00 per mensem. He put up his residence at Room No.10
of the Chinese Apartment House at 293 Hankow Road, when he
shared with two of his friends, Tsau Ching Feng and Yang Hoong
Sung (楊鴻順) also a Detective in the employ of the Tai Dao
Government.

The room was first rented by Tsau Ching Feng. On June
1st. 1938, Chang Zeng Kwang resigned from the Detective Bureau
in Pootung owing to poor health. On the same date, under the
instructions from the Headquarters in Pootung, Tsau Ching Feng
moved to 76 Yung Ching Lee off Jessfield Road, .O.., whilst
Yang Hoong Sung moved to Pootung and Chang Zeng Kwang took the
lease of the room.

On his savings he planned to enter the rice business in
partnership with his friend Kau Yao Ling (郭玉麟) a rice
merchant of Tseng Ying Sah Village near Kiangyin, who comes
occasionally to Shanghai with a cargo of rice for sale.
From the above it would be seen that allegations of the
Russian informer that Chang Zeng Kwang was the Commander of
the Chinese Mobile Unit, who had just arrived in Shanghai for
the purpose of purchasing firearms and who conducted negotia-
tions with him, are entirely without foundation.

As to regard to one Zong Foong (尚楓) 3rd arrested
man, the Russian informer stated that Zong had approached
his Chinese informer one Lieu Koong Hai (劉公海) regarding

该房间最初由赵俊峯租用。1938年6月1日，张成光因健康不佳辞去了浦东侦探局的职务。同日，根据浦东总部的指示，赵俊峯搬至兆丰公园路（Jessfield Road）附近的永庆里（Yung Ching Lee）76号，而杨鸿顺搬往浦东，张成光则承接了该房间的租约。

他计划用积蓄与朋友郭玉麟（Kau Yao Ling）合伙经营大米生意，郭玉麟是江阴附近曾营沙村（Tseng Ying Sah Village）的大米商人，偶尔会运一批大米到上海出售。
由此可见，俄罗斯线人指控张成光是中国流动部队指挥官，刚抵沪旨在购买枪支并与他进行谈判的说法，完全毫无根据。

为中国流动部队购买枪支一事接触其中方线人刘公海（Lieu Koong Hai），
后来由刘介绍给他。

尚枫首先开始与他谈判购买四十打毛瑟枪。

尚枫随后断然否认了俄罗斯和中国线人的指控，并陈述
说他实际上接触刘公海是希望通过他找一份工作。他于1938年1月
通过杭州政府职员唐伯顺（Mr. Tang）的介绍初次认识刘公海。1938年5月，
他在法租界再次见到刘，当听说刘在虹口区日本宪兵队手下
获得了一份侦探职位时，他便询问刘是否也能为他弄到一份类似的工作。
刘回答说他会试试看能帮什么忙，同时让他去拍半打照片，
解释说任何向维新政府申请职位的人都需要自行提供照片。

不再向他索要照片。侦探于1938年7月6日走访了该照相馆，
核实了尚枫的陈述。侦探支付30美分后，从照相馆取走了六张
护照尺寸的照片。

Formerly I was a circus trouper, travelling from one
nation to another, and am now residing at 59 Chusan Road,
Hongkew, the home of my Russian friend, one named Tretiakow.

I came to Shanghai in June 1937, with the intention to
find some capitalist and with whom to form a circus in Shanghai.
At that time I resided at 43 Siau Tao Yuen, French Concession.

In Sept., one named Zong, native of Shantung, and some
others, hearing I was a famous circus trouper, called on me
at the above address, whereupon I began to be acquainted with
the man Zong. Since then, Zong Fong frequented my address
and asked me to teach him how to play magic. He also hoped
me successfully forming a circus in Shanghai so that he would
procure a job and work under me. This I promised him.

Owing to the present situation I am unable to have all
the machines and other instruments used in the circus, removed
from Tientsin to Shanghai, therefore my proposal of operating
a circus remains unsuccessful till the present time.

In mid-Aug. last year, I encountered on Avenue Joffre,
my friend, Tretiakow, Russian, with whom I became acquainted
for the past 10 years. Tretiakow invited me to his home and
to have a talk with him. About a month afterwards I met
Tretiakow again and he informed me he was employed as a watch
of a certain factory in Hongkew, at a monthly pay of $100.
However, he later lost this employment due to his illness.

Several days afterwards Tretiakow asked me to remove and
live with him in Hongkew in order to help him in spying the
movements of Chinese troops.

以下为刘公海（Lieu Koong Hai）的陈述，46岁，已婚。
直隶（Chilhi）籍人士，由警探宋秉宗（Soong Ping Tsung）
于1938年7月11日在中央捕房总部（C.B.H.Q.）(C.1)录取，由书记员徐（Hsu）翻译。

以前我是马戏团演员，周游列国，现在居住在虹口中山路59号，即我的俄国朋友捷季亚科夫（Tretiakow）的家中。

我于1937年6月来到上海，打算寻找一位资本家，与其在上海组建一个马戏团。当时我居住在法租界小桃园43号。

9月，一位名叫宗（Zong）的山东籍男子和其他一些人，听说我是著名的马戏团演员，便到上述地址拜访我，于是我开始与宗相识。此后，宗方（Zong Fong，音译）经常光顾我的住处，并要求我教他变魔术。他还希望我在上海成功组建马戏团，以便他能谋得一份工作，在我手下做事。我答应了他。

由于目前的局势，我无法将马戏团使用的所有机械和其他器械从天津运到上海，因此我经营马戏团的提议至今未能成功。

去年8月中旬，我在霞飞路遇到了我的朋友、俄国人捷季亚科夫，我与他相识已有10年。捷季亚科夫邀请我去他家与他谈话。大约一个月后，我再次见到捷季亚科夫，他告诉我他在虹口某家工厂当看守，月薪100美元。然而，后来他因病失去了这份工作。

几天后，捷季亚科夫要求我搬去虹口与他同住，以帮助他监视中国军队的动向。

1938年5月的一天，宗丰（Zong Foong）来到我的住处，
请我购买枪械。听到这个请求后，我询问他购买的目的，
他说他是代表“流动小组”（Mobile Unit）的成员行事。然而，
我拒绝了他的请求。在我们交谈期间，特里亚科夫（Tretiakow）也在场。
宗丰离开后，特里亚科夫告诉我，他刚才只是想查明中国流动小组的活动情况，
因为他的叔叔在日本领事馆工作。他还告诉我，如果我们协助日本人查办此类案件，
日本人会给予我们重赏，因此如果宗丰下次再来，我可以答应他的请求，
因为他（特里亚科夫）会设法将其诱捕。

第二天，宗丰再次来拜访我，当时特里亚科夫也在场。
宗丰随即问特里亚科夫是否有枪械出售。特里亚科夫立即予以肯定答复，
并询问宗丰需要多少。宗丰回答说，他需要4打，每支枪配100发子弹。
他还告诉这位俄国人，每支枪械他愿意支付130美元。这位俄国人答应了这一价格，
但告诉宗丰在下一次会面之前准备好钱款。

从那时起，我和我的俄国朋友每天都在我家中等候宗丰再次来访。

然而，直到6月27日宗丰才露面，当时他与另一名姓张的人一同前来。
随后我们进行了谈判。谈判结果是商定了一个价格，即一支可发射20发的毛瑟手枪售价140美元。
我们让宗丰带着真正的买家再来

The following is the statement of LEE YU NOONG 李雨農, 40, M/Clerk,
native of Anhwei taken by me D.S.I. Soong Ping Tsung
at Gala on the 5.7.38 and interpreted by Clerk Ho

I am a native of Tiao Hsien, Anhwei, residing at Room 18,
House 293, Hankow Road. My past is as follows : -
After studying for 8 years, I became a merchant for 5 or 6
years. Then, I became a teacher in one of the farm schools for
over 3 years. In 1929, I came to Shanghai with Bau Kwai Tsung
and put up residence in the house of a friend, Zung Han Ching,
who formerly lived at Fa Tuh Li, S.Chengtu Road, now at House 7,
Nyi Woo Li, Rue Adm.Bayle, F/C. In April, 1930, I succeeded in
passing the examination for candidates to appointments of Court
Registrars, and soon became employed at $80 per month. Then I
moved to a house in Woo Keng Li, N.Chekiang Road, from where I
again moved to 293 Hankow Road at the outbreak of hostilities,
which caused also the removal of the late S.S.D.Court to Peking
Road. Soon the Court moved to Weihaiwei Road. I made every
effort to rent a house in its vicinity so that I could reduce my
locomotion expenses, but the results were nil.
I am sure there must be some misunderstanding which caused
my arrest. Besides, my position with the Court, I have no
connections, whatsoever, with other public bodies. Four others
were arrested in the same Room No.10, but I don't know them. The
Russian et al never met me before. My position with the Court
is purely clerical and my duties are limited to that of recording
etc. Since the end of last year, I worked with Judge Fee Ling.
Frequently, things could not be completed during office hours and
necessitated working in evenings too. This is the truth.
LEE YU NOONG.

以下为李雨農（LEE YU NOONG）的陈述，男，40岁，书记员，安徽籍，
由副督察宋秉忠（D.S.I. Soong Ping Tsung）于1938年7月5日在加拉监狱（Gala）录取，
由何书记员翻译

我是安徽调县（Tiao Hsien）人，居住在汉口路293号18室。我的过往经历如下：-
读书八年后，我经商五六年。之后，我在一所农校任教三年多。
1929年，我与鲍桂宗（Bau Kwai Tsung）一同来到上海，
住在一位朋友钟汉清（Zung Han Ching）家中，
钟以前住在成都南路法华里（Fa Tuh Li），现住在法租界贝当路（Rue Adm.Bayle）宜武里7号。
1930年4月，我成功通过了法院书记官候选人的考试，
不久即以月薪80元受聘。随后我搬至浙江北路吴兴里的一处住宅，
战事爆发后，我又搬至汉口路293号，这也导致前特区地方法院迁至南京路。
不久法院又迁至威海卫路。我曾尽力在法院附近租房以减少交通费用，但未果。
我相信我的被捕一定是由于某种误会。此外，除了我在法院的职位外，
我与任何其他公共机构没有任何联系。另有四人在同一10号房间被捕，但我不认识他们。
那位俄国人等人以前从未见过我。我在法院的职位纯粹是文书性质的，
我的职责仅限于记录等事务。自去年年底以来，我一直在费灵（Fee Ling）法官手下工作。
经常有些事务无法在办公时间内完成，因此晚上也需要加班。这是事实。
李雨農。

I am a candy dealer, residing at the upstairs front room
of the Tientsin Hospital, Rue Hsu, F/C. I took my family to
Shanghai in 1933, and since that year, I have been leading the
life of a dealer, my wife working for people in sewing etc. and
my daughter having an employment with the Sino-Japanese Cotton
Mill. Soon, I became employed as a secret watchman at the Sung
Sing First Mill. During 1935, Li Yau Tsing, Vai Chi Ming and
myself put up a capital and established a bathhouse, named the
Tsing Suen Sz, in Chapei, which ceased operation at the outbreak
of hostilities. During Nov.1937, I became acquainted with Zau
Tsing Foong, through whose recommendation, I obtained the
position of accountant at the Pah Kyi Transportation Co. which
closed down in Feb.1938. Then I eked out a living by dealing in
candy. During my employment with the Pah Kyi Transportation Co.
I made the acquaintance of one Tsang Zung Kwong, employee of
Woo Tsoong Co. As latter was ill, I paid him a visit on 30.6.38
at the Woo Tsoong Co. Building, accompanied by Tsang Zu Daung.
Soon, after my arrival, two unknown Chinese and one Russian came
into Room 10 and stayed for awhile. I learned that they were
connected with firms in H'kew and having considerable influence
in Japanese circles. On the following morning I went to Room 10 to
request their assistance to obtain me a job in H'kew. Soon, I was
arrested together with Li and Zong, both strangers to me.
This is the truth.

TSAI WEI ZIEN.

由宋副督察（D.S.I. Seong）于1938年7月5日在科尔监狱（Col.）录取，
由姚书记员翻译

我是一名糖果商，居住在法租界徐家汇路天津医院楼上的一间前屋。
1933年我携家眷来到上海，自那年起，我一直过着商贩的生活，
我的妻子为他人做缝纫等工作，女儿在中日棉纱厂任职。
不久，我受雇为松盛第一纱厂的秘密看守。
1935年间，李友庆（Li Yau Tsing）、魏志明（Vai Chi Ming）和我出资
在闸北开设了一家名为“清顺池”（Tsing Suen Sz）的浴室，
该浴室在战事爆发时停止营业。1937年11月，我通过赵庆丰（Zau Tsing Foong）的介绍，
获得了百记运输公司（Pah Kyi Transportation Co.）会计的职位，
该公司于1938年2月倒闭。此后我靠贩卖糖果维持生计。
在百记运输公司任职期间，我结识了伍松公司（Woo Tsoong Co.）的一名雇员曾仲光（Tsang Zung Kwong）。
因后者生病，我于1938年6月30日在曾祖堂（Tsang Zu Daung）的陪同下，
前往伍松公司大楼探望他。我不久到达后，两名不知名的中国人和一名俄国人进入10号房间并停留了一会儿。
我得知他们与虹口区的商行有关联，并在日本圈子中具有相当大的影响力。
次日早晨，我前往10号房间，请求他们帮助我在虹口找一份工作。
不久，我与李和宗两人一同被捕，而我与他们二人均不相识。
这是事实。

蔡蔚然。

I am a coal broker, residing upstairs of the hot water shop
at the entrance of Woo Hsing Li Alleyway, Rue Adm. Bayle, F/C. I
came to Shanghai in 1930, and became employed as an inspector at
the Hwa Ching Cigarette Factory through the efforts of Tsang Voong
Lou. In 1933, this factory ceased operation, and I moved to Wong
Ka Moh Deu, Nantao, to take up coal business. At the outbreak of
hostilities last year I moved to my former address on Rue Adm.
Bayle, F/C, still working as a coal dealer. I did not know Tsang
Kwong Zung until the 30.6.38 when my friend Tsai Wei Zien
accompanied me to pay a visit to Tsang at his home on Hankow Road,
as the latter had been ill. We went to Tsang's house at Room 10,
Woo Foong Co. Hankow Road, where after a while, one Russian and two
Chinese, name unknown, came into the room, (one of the Chinese was
Zong Foong, which I learned later). They came to discuss things
regarding recommending people to appointments of detectives in
Hongkew District, and that the recruits would function on 1.7.38.
As I was eager to obtain such a position I went to this room again
on the next day, 1.7.38, hoping that they would employ me as well.
However, at about 2 p.m. Police arrived and placed us under arrest.
One named Li was also arrested, but I do not know him. This is the
truth.

TSANG ZU DAUNG.

张树棠。

The following is the statement of TSANG ZUNG KYONG [签名], 37, H/Ex-watchman,
native of Shantung taken by me D.S.I. Soong P. Ts.
at C.1. on the 5.7.38 and interpreted by Clerk Yao

I have been living for four months in Room 10, Woo Foong
Co. Bdg, House 293, Hankow Road, which was engaged by Tsu Tsing
Foong, as a temporary office. I am unemployed at present.
I came to Shanghai in 1926, when after spending over two
months trying to obtain a position, I finally became employed as
a watchman at the Asiatic Petroleum Co. Canton Road, through the
kind recommendation of one, Liang Wei Daung, whose native town
was also Shantung. Shortly afterwards in an effort to obtain the
position of a police watchman in the International Settlement
my cousin, Tsang Tsoong Zung (C.P.C.2108) took me to Police HQ's.
and requested Mr. Yao, D.C.(Chinese) for permission to register
my name with the S.M.P. so that I could be included in the
"Waiting list" for prospective appointments to C.P.W.'s vacancies.
I did not intend to work in the A.P.C. permanently and it was my
ambition to be a C.P.W. Some two months later, I tendered my
resignation and terminated my service with the A.P.C. owing to
prolonged illness. After being confined abed for about two months
I became well again, and soon, through the efforts of my friend,
Tsu Hoong Tuh, I became watchman at the Zih Tung Co. Wharf, with
offices at House 44, Zung Chih Li, Dent Road. With this firm I
served for over a year, after which I finally received a notice
from Mr. Yao, Police Commissioner, appointing me to be a C.P.W.

in his presence.
    When the money was paid he asked the Russian to give
him a receipt for it which he did. The receipt reads as
follows:-

    I received in advance a sum of $50.00 for ......(illegible

Police Search Patrols
Continue Activity
In Louza

Some five Chinese suspected of
having taken part in anti-Japan-
ese activities here who were
seized on the premises of the Woo
Foong Trading Company on Han-
kow Road yesterday, did not ap-
pear in the First District Court
this morning, as expected. In-
stead, rumor had it at court that
the men are in custody of the
Japanese Consular Police, though
this could not be verified.
First reports stated that the
raid was made by Japanese, but
later it was learned that SMP de-
tectives did the work. It was also
denied that a Russian was im-
plicated, but it is understood that
anti-Japanese propaganda was
seized.
Meanwhile the Reserve Unit
assisted by the Russian Regiment,
SVC, continued today their sys-
tematic campaign against ter-
rorists in the Settlement, careful-
ly searching blocks of houses,
particularly in the Louza District.
The searches are on a scale un-
precedented in the city's annals.
Blocks and alleys are roped off,
pedestrians are searched day and
night, and the riot vans stand by.
Many hotels and lodging houses
are being raided in the down-
town department store area by
patrols in steel vests and guards
with bayonets, in search of as-
sassin-suspects, arms, bombs, etc.
A number of suspicious characters
have been detained but little in-
formation has as yet been got.
In Chinese circles there are re-
ports that a large number of
guerillas has filtered into the city,
but police discount these allega-
tions. They are, nevertheless,
hunting grimly for the gang of
assassins that has been bury here
for several weeks.

Lile

约五名涉嫌在此参与反日活动的中国人，昨日在汉口路伍丰贸易公司（Woo Foong Trading Company） premises 被抓获，今早未按预期出现在第一特区法院。相反，法院内有传言称这些人被日本领事馆警察拘留，但这无法得到证实。
最初的报告称突袭由日本人实施，但后来得知是由上海公共租界工部局警务处（SMP）侦探执行的。也有人否认有俄国人卷入，但据悉反日宣传品被查获。
与此同时，后备队（Reserve Unit）在义勇军（SVC）俄国团的协助下，今天继续其在租界内对恐怖分子的系统性打击行动，仔细搜查成片街区，特别是老闸区（Louza District）。搜查规模在该市历史上前所未有。街区和巷弄被封锁，行人日夜受到搜身，防暴车随时待命。许多位于市中心百货商店区域的旅馆和寄宿处正遭到身穿钢背心、手持刺刀的警卫巡逻队的突袭，以搜寻刺客嫌疑人、武器、炸弹等。多名可疑人物被拘留，但迄今获取的情报甚少。
在华界圈子中有报告称大量游击队员已潜入市区，但警方对这些说法不予采信。尽管如此，警方仍在严厉搜捕已在此潜伏数周的刺客团伙。
